cases.title: Investor, cloud vendor and revenue-share recipient
cases.summary: Microsoft finances OpenAI; OpenAI buys Azure services and generates reported Microsoft revenue.
cases.insight: Separate contracted demand, recognized revenue and receivables. Growth financed by new capital can be real, yet remains sensitive to the lab's eventual cash generation.
cases.limitation: No tracing of identical dollars. Microsoft's investment valuation is not investment cash, and recognized revenue is not profit.

cases.title: Funding customers of your own cloud
cases.summary: Amazon funds both OpenAI and Anthropic while both commit to long-term AWS capacity.
cases.insight: The commercial and financing exposures can weaken together if AI customers cannot cover compute costs from external demand.
cases.limitation: Different horizons and instruments; no valid single 'circulating dollars' total. Deliveries, conditions and funding milestones differ.

cases.title: Two investors, one NVIDIA-powered cloud route
cases.summary: Microsoft and NVIDIA back Anthropic, which contracts Azure capacity on NVIDIA systems.
cases.insight: One relationship supports model funding, cloud demand and accelerator demand. Hardware capacity alone does not reveal NVIDIA's transaction revenue.
cases.limitation: The supplier leg is documented technologically but not monetarily sized; Anthropic's other chip platforms diversify dependence.

cases.title: Supplier, shareholder and buyer of spare capacity
cases.summary: NVIDIA sells GPUs, invests in CoreWeave and backstops qualifying spare cloud capacity. Contract-backed loans finance deployment.
cases.insight: The key test is third-party utilization versus vendor support, alongside interest, GPU life, collateral and delivery obligations.
cases.limitation: Backstop value is conditional and cannot be added to equity, debt capacity or customer contract values as current sales.

cases.title: A hyperscaler contract becomes financing capacity
cases.summary: Microsoft contracts capacity; NVIDIA provides capital and hardware; lenders advance against deployed GPUs and customer cash flows.
cases.insight: Customer commitments can finance expansion into new enterprise workloads. Watch how much growth relies on deposits, refinancing and a few creditworthy buyers.
cases.limitation: The named Microsoft contract and July secured loan are not proven to be the same collateral pool. This is a financing chain, not a proven closed loop.

cases.title: Chip supplier underwrites the infrastructure tenant
cases.summary: NVIDIA's SB Energy guarantee supports OpenAI's future campus leases and an overwhelmingly NVIDIA-based site.
cases.insight: Credit support can unlock physical construction before tenant cash flows mature. The supplier gains deployment opportunities while accepting long-lived contingent risk.
cases.limitation: Ohio and Oracle projects are separate routes, not one contract. Guarantees are contingent exposure, not money already transferred.

cases.title: Vendor financing → GPU cloud → hardware → vendor
cases.classification: Documented capital/commercial feedback; individual dollars not traced
cases.analysis: NVIDIA supplies equity and a conditional capacity backstop while CoreWeave builds an NVIDIA-based cloud, including Dell racks. Lenders convert assets and contracts into funding. Vendor revenue, equity, and total contract values are different accounting objects; summing them overstates final demand.
watch: Operating cash generated from customers unaffiliated with equipment vendors
Cash actually drawn versus facility headline
Capacity utilization, GPU resale value and debt amortization
Revenue earned versus remaining contractual backlog
cases.risk: Supplier, investor, customer and collateral exposure can correlate; this does not by itself establish fraudulent round-tripping.
cases.summary: NVIDIA supplies equity and a conditional capacity backstop while CoreWeave builds an NVIDIA-based cloud, including Dell racks. Lenders convert assets and contracts into funding. Vendor revenue, equity, and total contract values are different accounting objects; summing them overstates final demand. CoreWeave also reports financing from unnamed equipment and software vendors.
cases.insight: Watch: Operating cash generated from customers unaffiliated with equipment vendors; Cash actually drawn versus facility headline; Capacity utilization, GPU resale value and debt amortization; Revenue earned versus remaining contractual backlog.
cases.limitation: Supplier, investor, customer and collateral exposure can correlate; this does not by itself establish fraudulent round-tripping.

cases.title: Chip revenue → foundry → tools and construction

watch: Foundry capacity utilization and customer prepayments
Equipment backlog conversion, cancellations and cash collection
HBM capacity additions versus realized prices
Customer concentration and export controls

cases.title: Cloud procurement → fuel cells → shares back to the customer
cases.classification: Documented non-cash customer incentive alongside procurement
cases.analysis: Bloom’s Oracle arrangement includes both equipment deployment and a cashlessly exercised share incentive. Project financing can place a capital provider between the cloud customer and equipment vendor. This is an economic feedback link, not proof that the identical cash was recycled.
watch: Revenue reductions from customer consideration
Equipment versus service margin and replacement obligations
Project-level debt, ownership and power-purchase terms
Signed projects versus broad capital frameworks
cases.risk: Equity incentives and headline financing frameworks can make headline demand look larger than near-term, independent cash receipts.

cases.title: AI cloud → project developer → debt, tax equity and fuel cells

Interest coverage after maintenance and service obligations

cases.title: Cloud and utility spending reaches sites and local contractors
cases.classification: Long-term leases and ordinary construction spending
cases.analysis: A cloud tenant supports long-duration data-center rent, which helps finance property buildout. Utility spending reaches named local engineers and contractors. These are additional recipients of AI-linked expenditure, not automatically financial loops.
watch: Prepayments, rent credits and actual billed capacity
Lease duration versus tenant/customer contract duration
Construction cost overruns and power permits
Parent guarantees versus project-only recourse

methodology: Tier 1: model labs and major cloud providers. Tier 2: compute operators, hardware and direct suppliers. Tier 3: manufacturing enablers, power, sites, contractors and project financing. Cases include upstream links when needed for context.
Relationships are based on named counterparties in primary sources. Some describe an established supplier route without a disclosed invoice or payment.
Paid investments, outstanding borrowing, signed commitments, frameworks, conditional guarantees and recognized revenue retain separate labels. No aggregate capital-flow total is calculated.
The same dollar is not traced through the system. Interdependence can amplify a spending shock, but is not proof of fictitious revenue.
